newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ugandan-trained "Tutsi legion" beat Zaire - Monde.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan-trained "Tutsi legion" beat Zaire - Monde.

text.p: A Ugandan-trained "Tutsi Legion" of as many as 15,000 men has been the main force in rebel leader Laurent Kabila's so-far sucessful drive to oust Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko, the French daily Le Monde said on Monday.

The well-informed newspaper said French and Belgian intelligence agencies agreed the force, recruited in Uganda, Eritrea and Burundi, had enjoyed direct logistics support from the Ugandan government army during certain phases of the offensive, including the capture of Kisangani in March.
France, which long backed Mobbutu, has several times accused Uganda and Rwanda of direct intervention in the conflict, accusations denied by the two African states.
The core of Kabila's forces was known to be recruited from among Zairean-born Tutsis who revolted last year, saying the Zairean government discriminated against them.

Le Monde, quoting the intelligence sources, said the only time the Tutsi force suffered serious casualties was during operations around Kisangani when it lost up to 3,000 dead and wounded, mostly at the hands of foreign mercenaries and Hutu former Rwandan government soldiers.
The biggest losses were caused by Serb-manned MiL-24 helicopter gunships using air-to-ground missiles and napalm cannisters, the newspaper said.
"Raids," a French magazine specialised in guns and military afffairs, published a long article about Western mercenaries who it said served as advisers to Mobutu's forces from December to March.
It said they numbered 33, mostly French but also including an Italian, a Chilean and a Belgian.

Most were veterans of ageing French "dog of War" Bob Denard's adventures in the Comoro Islands and elsewhere, said the magazine. which published numerous photos, all of them with the faces of the mercenaries blanked out.
Denard is currently banned from leaving France.

The magazine said the mercenaries were consistently abandoned by the Zairean troops they trained and were able to avoid capture or death several times by being evacuated, usually at the last minute, by a mercenary American pilot flying a twin-engined Andover and identified only as Roland.
Relations between the Western mercenaries and a larger group of about 100 Serb mercenaries were poor, the magazine said, adding they did not work together.
France has always denied any hand in recruiting the mercenaries to back Mobutu, a Paris ally.
But critics of Paris's African policy have insisted they were indeed recruited with the support of some French secret service group, possibly without full government clearance.
